clue.text: Old secessionist, I burnt with rage, festering, hot inside

indicators.note: the word before it is to be placed within the rearranged letters
a festering wound is going bad and changing, so the words before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A furious rebel from history, seething with resentment over something burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Antiburghers were the faction of the Scottish Secession Church who refused the burgess oath in 1747.
explanation.definitionFit: An Antiburgher belonged to a breakaway Scottish church party, so the term names a historical seceder.

clue.text: Former skipper but opener for Notts

parts.note: bar and but both mean except, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, so only the initial letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the first letter of Notts

explanation.surface: A one-time captain who was nonetheless an opening batsman for Nottinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipper looks like a cricket captain beside Notts (Nottinghamshire, a county cricket side), but Chambers lists skipper as obsolete slang for a barn, a vagrant's sleeping place.
explanation.definitionFit: In old slang a skipper was a barn or outhouse where tramps slept, so the two words once shared a meaning.

clue.text: Lesser followers? Homer's fourth taking the lead I'll follow

indicators.note: the letter in fourth place moves from its own spot to the very front of the word

parts.note: a homer is a homing pigeon; its fourth letter is the one that moves
the letter I is added at the end

explanation.surface: A question about Homer's minor imitators, with someone promising to follow in fourth place.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer is not the poet but a homing pigeon: its fourth letter, E, jumps to the front to make EPIGON, and I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigoni are inferior successors or imitators of a great generation, after the sons of the Seven against Thebes.

clue.text: Moses initially is found beside biblical river — did it involve some gambling?

indicators.note: found beside places the pieces next to each other in a row
initially points to the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the first letter of Moses
taken as written
the Tigris is one of the rivers of Eden in Genesis

explanation.surface: Moses found beside a river in the Bible; did his story involve a wager?
explanation.walkthrough: Moses suggests the baby among the bulrushes, but that river was the Nile; only his initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistigris is a card game, a form of poker played with a joker or blank card, so gambling was part of it.

clue.text: Grim deity showing want to dominate church

indicators.note: in a down entry, dominating means sitting on top, so the first piece comes above the second

parts.note: want is a dialect name for the mole, the burrowing animal
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A stern god displaying a desire to rule over the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Want reads as desire, but Chambers gives it as an old word for a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: Molech is the Canaanite god associated in the Bible with child sacrifice, a fittingly grim deity.

clue.text: Suite surrounding queen with happiness

indicators.note: surrounding tells us one word goes round the other, here the last word round the queen

parts.note: seel is an archaic word for happiness or good fortune
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Hotel rooms wrapped around a queen, plus some contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Suite looks like a set of rooms; here it is the older sense of a succession or train of things following.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite in its sense of a following sequence matches a sequel, what comes after and follows on.

clue.text: One's usually drunk when tucking into snifter

indicators.note: something tucking into another goes inside it

parts.note: a snifter is a small drink, a tot
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone who is normally intoxicated whenever they get stuck into a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's usually drunk' reads as a person who is tipsy; it really means a thing that is usually drunk, raised and drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a tribute marked by everyone drinking, so it is something normally drunk.

clue.text: Like chemical solutions often shortening life in medicine container (7, two words)

indicators.note: in places the shortened word within the box that follows

parts.note: an inro is a small Japanese box for pills, hung from the sash

indicators.note: shortening a word cuts off its tail

parts.note: vita is Latin for life

explanation.surface: Chemical solutions often cut life short inside a container of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: An inro is a small Japanese box carried at the waist for pills and medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: In vitro means in glass, in a test tube, which is where chemical solutions usually sit.

clue.text: Basic food for soldiers identified by rank

definitions.text: food for soldiers identified by rank
definitions.meaning: second meaning: old military slang for bread, eaten by rankers

explanation.surface: Plain rations for troops, recognised by their stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooty, from Hindi roti, was army slang for bread; 'identified by rank' marks the soldiers as other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means full of roots, hence radical or basic, and separately was soldiers' slang for bread.

clue.text: Where some Vectian folk may be found leaving out note for artificer?

indicators.note: leaving out says a letter must be dropped from the place just named

parts.words: Where some Vectian folk may be found
parts.note: a Vectian is an Isle of Wight native (Vectis was its Roman name), so some live in Ventnor, a town on the island
N stands for note

explanation.surface: A question about where Isle of Wight people live, skipping a note, posed for a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ventnor is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight; drop one N from IN VENTNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled maker or contriver, which is what an inventor is.

clue.text: Rich cake, new, with a part that's thickly iced on

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
the North and South Poles are the parts of the earth under thick ice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rich cake, freshly made, with one section heavily iced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thickly iced' suggests cake icing, but it points to a polar ice cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A napoleon is a rich pastry of layered puff pastry and cream, a mille-feuille.

clue.text: What'll form link, physically? Name certain circles

indicators.note: circles is a verb here: one word goes round another

parts.note: pos is short for positive, meaning certain
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A question about bonding, followed by naming some social circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'physically' means in the body: a pons is an anatomical bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a pons is a bridge of tissue joining two parts, especially the pons in the brainstem.

clue.text: Marine echinoderm exhibiting wiggly pertness sailor's after

indicators.note: something wiggly twists about, so the following word's letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor; the 's means 'is', so TAR comes after

explanation.surface: A sea creature showing wriggling cheekiness, pursued by a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sailor's after' reads as 'the sailor is after', placing TAR at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent star is a brittlestar, an echinoderm with thin snake-like arms.

clue.text: Poet's spun line in earth recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the result is read the other way
in puts the single letter inside the following word

parts.note: dirt is earth or soil
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A poet's yarn has a line buried in soil and remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' signals a Spenserian form: trild is his spelling of trilled, meaning twirled or rolled.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used trild as the past tense of trill, to turn or twirl, matching spun.

clue.text: Peacock's name (not the first) for duck

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the middle name of the novelist Thomas ... Peacock
second meaning: nil, a score of zero

explanation.surface: A peacock's pet name, not its first one, for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Peacock is the Romantic satirist Thomas Love Peacock, not the bird. A duck in cricket and love in tennis both mean nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis term for zero, and a duck is a cricketer's zero score, so both mean nothing.

clue.text: Callow youth at home with related group mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: at home means in
a genus is a group of related species

explanation.surface: An inexperienced lad living at home with most of his relations.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingenu is the masculine of ingénue.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenu is a naive, artless young man, which is a callow youth.

clue.text: One who's posed a simple task

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a model who sits for a portrait
second meaning: something easy, such as an easy catch

explanation.walkthrough: 'posed' reads as 'set' a task, but it is about sitting for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is a model sitting for a painter, and colloquially an easy chance or task.

clue.text: H. Corbett? 'E junked bit of kitchen metalware

indicators.note: junked letters have been thrown away in a heap, out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Harry H. Corbett threw out a kitchen gadget, in Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry H. Corbett played the junk dealer in Steptoe and Son, so 'junked' and the dropped-H 'E suit him.
explanation.definitionFit: A brochette is a small metal skewer for cooking meat, an item of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: At Le Gavroche, the water used in thickening for rolls

indicators.note: used in puts one ingredient inside the other

parts.note: a roux is a flour and butter base for thickening sauces
Le Gavroche is a French restaurant in London, so 'the water' is put into French as l'eau

explanation.surface: A smart French restaurant adds water to a sauce base for its bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: The article counts too: 'the water' in French is l'eau, giving four letters. Fittingly, Le Gavroche was founded by the Roux brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouleaux are cylindrical rolls, such as a stack of coins wrapped in paper.

clue.text: Smart (?) milliner fashioned items for clothing on demand

indicators.note: clothing wraps around, so the rearranged word goes round the abbreviation
something fashioned is made into a new shape, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
OD is the abbreviation for on demand

explanation.surface: A hatmaker produced garments to order.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart (?) hints the word means a fashionable dressmaker, with the query because the smartness is the clothes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a maker of fashionable hats or dresses, so a milliner of stylish goods.

clue.text: Delilah learning how to finish off 'knight' cut coiffure

parts.note: lore is learning or know-how

indicators.note: to finish off asks for the final letter of each of the words after it

parts.note: the last letter of knight
the last letter of cut
the last letter of coiffure

explanation.surface: Delilah learns how to cut a strongman's hair, ending a knight's locks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Delilah cutting Samson's hair, which is why 'cut coiffure' looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorette is a kept woman or courtesan, and Delilah is the archetypal seductive temptress.

clue.text: Twice as much ordered with twice coming in

indicators.note: coming in puts the middle words inside the first one

parts.note: told means ordered, as in 'told to leave'
with is taken twice, as W and as of, which means with in 'a man of courage'

explanation.surface: Double the amount ordered, with two portions arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Twofold means double, so twice as large or twice as much.

clue.text: Contact sport is about number united falling down

indicators.note: about means around, so the word before it goes round the two that follow

parts.note: RU is rugby union
taken as written
NO is the abbreviation for number
U is the abbreviation for united

explanation.surface: A rough sport concerns a team that keeps falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous can mean ruined or dilapidated, a building that is falling down.

clue.text: Tiny marine organism hiding in stones

indicators.note: a hiding is a beating, and a beaten word is knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A little sea creature concealed among pebbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding in' wants a hidden word, but the answer is not in a row inside stones; hiding is a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Seston is the mass of tiny organisms and particles floating in water, plankton among them.

clue.text: Heavy blow accompanying explosive? Bandage required

indicators.note: accompanying puts the following item alongside, after the first

parts.note: a swat is a heavy blow
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: Hit hard while carrying a bomb, a dressing is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is a wrapping or bandage, a band of cloth wound round something.

clue.text: Bear by the sound of it in Aussie eucalypt

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is judged by pronunciation, not spelling

parts.note: bear means carry

explanation.surface: A bear seems to be up an Australian gum tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The karri is a tall eucalyptus of Western Australia, valued for its hard timber.

clue.text: Upset, tad worried? Not I — this may counter venomous attack

indicators.note: Not tells us the letter named must be removed
upset things are knocked over and jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
worried less the I

explanation.surface: A little anxious about a bite? Not me: this remedy will handle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Adderwort, bistort, was traditionally believed to cure snakebite, so it counters a venomous bite.

clue.text: Government department pay, year short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the letter named is missing

parts.note: to defray is to pay costs
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A ministry's wages are a year in arrears.
explanation.walkthrough: Defra is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Defra is the acronym of a British ministry, so it is the name of a government department.

clue.text: Poet's displaying shock, making haste to grab attention

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to hie is to hasten
ear means attention, as in 'lend an ear'

explanation.surface: A poet looks startled, rushing to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock is a shock of hair; hearie is Spenser's spelling of hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's hearie means hairy, and a shock is a thick mass of hair, so it displays a shock.

clue.text: County clubs (rather on the thin side?)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English Midlands county
second meaning: sticks, rather slender for clubs

explanation.walkthrough: County clubs suggests cricket teams; a staff is a stick, thinner than a cudgel, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffs is the common short form of Staffordshire, and staffs are poles that could serve as thin cudgels.

clue.text: Made it, that is entering one's personal area of control

indicators.note: entering means going inside the following abbreviation

parts.note: ff. stands for Latin fecerunt, 'they made it', on works of art
i.e. is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Succeeded, that is, by moving into one's own territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A fief is a feudal estate, and figuratively a domain under one person's control.

clue.text: Bring in plant shoot before end of autumn

parts.note: an ear is the seed-bearing spike of a cereal plant

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word after it

parts.note: the last letter of autumn

explanation.surface: Harvest a plant's growth before autumn ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to bring in money as income.

clue.text: Stagger after Scotch? Add this to get fit

parts.note: surface reading: a remedy or tonic that would make you healthy
setter's reading: the answer split as an instruction, an S joined to an IT, gives a word meaning fit, as clothes fit

explanation.surface: Reeling after a whisky, and told to take more to feel well.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed's note confirms the reverse reading: join S to IT to make SIT, and to sit is to fit, as a jacket sits well. Scotch also hints at a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoit is Scots for stagger or lurch, the gait of someone after too much Scotch whisky.

clue.text: NZ hooter curtailed score twice

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a run is a score in cricket
the shortened score is taken a second time

explanation.surface: A New Zealand horn cut short scores twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is an owl, not a car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruru is the morepork, a small New Zealand owl named for its call.

clue.text: Chlorate damaged opening for tendon maybe

indicators.note: damaged letters have been broken and put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spoiled chemical leaves a gap for a tendon.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochlea is a pulley-like anatomical structure through which a tendon passes, as in the eye socket.

clue.text: Like demanding demoiselle, former flame eating out with end of affaire

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the French word after it

parts.note: the last letter of affaire

explanation.surface: A fussy young lady, an old flame of mine, dining out, with the affair ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Demoiselle signals the French feminine form, exigeante rather than exigeant.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigeante is the feminine of exigeant, meaning exacting or demanding, as said of a woman.
